description: The line plot illustrates "Performance w.r.t. Temperature" by comparing the accuracy of three different methods across varying temperature values. The x-axis is labeled "Temperature" and features a linear scale ranging from 0.1 to 1.0, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.1. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy (Pass@8)" and uses a linear scale with visible tick marks ranging from 62.5 to 80.0 at intervals of 2.5. The "On-policy RL" method is represented by a solid yellow line with upward-pointing triangle markers; it begins at approximately 63.7 at a temperature of 0.1, rises to roughly 70.0 at 0.2, fluctuates with a notable drop to 67.3 at 0.7, reaches its peak at approximately 75.2 at 0.8, and ends at 73.5 at 1.0. The "LUFFY" method is depicted by a solid dark red line with star markers, starting at 76.2 at 0.1, experiencing a local peak of 78.8 at 0.2, dipping to 76.1 at 0.3 and 0.4, and generally trending upward to reach its highest values of approximately 80.5 at both 0.8 and 1.0, with a brief dip to 78.8 at 0.9. Finally, the "SFT" method is shown as a solid teal line with downward-pointing triangle markers; it begins at 76.2 at 0.1, steadily declines to a low of 70.0 at 0.5, sharply rebounds to 76.1 at 0.6, and then fluctuates before concluding at approximately 74.4 at 1.0.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates Pass@8 accuracy across varying generation temperatures, measured on the merged sets of AIME 2024 and AMC. The 'On-policy RL' line (yellow, triangle markers) shows a steady increase from approximately 63.0 at 0.1 to 75.0 at 0.8, followed by a slight decline to 73.0 at 1.0. The 'LUFFY' line (red, star markers) demonstrates consistent superiority, starting at 76.0 at 0.1 and peaking at 81.0 at 0.8, before stabilizing at 80.0 at 1.0. The 'SFT' line (teal, inverted triangle markers) begins at 73.0 at 0.1, dips sharply to 68.0 at 0.5, and recovers to 74.0 at 1.0, showing the most variability among the three methods. Overall, LUFFY consistently outperforms the other methods across all temperature settings, with On-policy RL showing the most significant improvement over time.
